payload.DEMAND_CHARGES.CALCULATION.TITLE: Demand Charges Calculation
payload.DEMAND_CHARGES.CALCULATION.TOU.DESC:
Demand charges are calculated differently in Summer and Non-Summer months.

Non-Summer months: Demand charges are based on the highest 15-minute usage recorded over the entire day (24 hours).
Summer months: demand charges include two components:
  • Demand Charge: Demand based on on-peak hours,
  • Facility Charge: Demand based on 24-hour usage.
Peak demand is the highest 15-minute power usage in a day, often occurring when several appliances run at the same time. Each day's peak is recorded and combined to calculate your total demand charge. Charts are for reference only.
payload.DEMAND_CHARGES.CALCULATION.TOU.PEAK_DESC: This charge is calculated using the highest 15-minute usage during on-peak hours each day. Only usage that occurs within the on-peak time window is considered.
payload.DEMAND_CHARGES.CALCULATION.TOU.PEAK_TITL: Demand based on peak hours (Summer only)

payload.DISAGG101_AIC.ALWAYS_ON.DESC: Always On includes "plugged-in" devices such as personal computers, monitors, printers, stereos, and televisions that consume energy even when they're turned off.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.BASE-LOAD.DESC: Base load includes "plugged-in" devices such as computers, monitors, printers, and televisions that consume energy even when they're turned off.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.COOKING.DESC: Cooking and food preparation appliances that consume significant electricity can be found in this category, including oven, stove, toaster, and toaster oven.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.COOLING.DESC: This includes common cooling appliances such as central air conditioner, split air conditioners, window air conditioners, fans and coolers.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.ELECTRIC_VEHICLE.DESC: This category includes the aggregate usage of all EVs at the home.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.ELECTRIC_WATER_HEATING.DES: Water heater includes all whole home water heaters (tanked and tankless) as well as specific use water heaters (geysers)
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.ENTERTAINMENT.DESC: Entertainment is comprised of two main appliance types: consumer electronics (TV, game console, stereo) and home computing (desktop, monitor, printer).
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.HEADLINE: Appliance Itemization Categories
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.LAUNDRY.DESC: Laundry consists of "wet washing" electric appliances, such as dishwasher, washing machine, and dryer.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.LIGHTING.DESC: This includes all lights in the home, from efficient LED bulbs to inefficient halogen bulbs, and everything in between.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.OPERATIONAL-LOAD.DESC: This includes all lights, from efficient LED bulbs to inefficient halogen bulbs, and everything in between, as well as refrigerators and other kitchen appliances.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.OPERATIONAL_LOAD.DESC: This includes all lights, from efficient LED bulbs to inefficient halogen bulbs, and everything in between, as well as refrigerators and other kitchen appliances.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.OTHER.DESC: These are appliances that are too small or infrequently used to be categorized separately. This includes mobile phones, vacuum cleaners, hair dryers, and curling irons.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.POOL_PUMP.DESC: Pool pumps have motors that keep your pool water filtered and clean year-round.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.REFRIGERATION.DESC: Refrigeration includes the aggregate usage of refrigerators and freezers in the home.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.SPACE_HEATING.DESC: Electric heating includes many different types of heaters: radiant, convection, fan, storage, underfloor, heat pumps, and the electric fan component of gas heating.
payload.DISAGG101_AIC.SUB_HEADLINE: We itemize your usage into 10 major appliance categories. You can track the usage of every single category over the course of the year and see how they change based on season, weather and your behavior. We display categories that consume a large amount of electricity, like Always On (baseload), Cooling and Electric Vehicle, based on the usage from your meter. We then take this usage to infer and estimate how much your other appliance categories, like laundry, cooking, lighting and entertainment, are consuming. Thus, through a combination of your actual usage and our rule-based model, we can compose a holistic picture of your total energy consumption.
payload.DISAGG101_AIE.ANSWER_1: Not really. Each appliance uses electricity in a unique manner - think of it like an appliance fingerprint. We detect and extract these "fingerprints" and convert the data into useful insights and recommendations.
payload.DISAGG101_AIE.ANSWER_2: Don't worry, we've got you covered. The insights we derive from each appliance in your home will change according to your actual usage patterns. So whether you go on vacation, buy a new appliance, or have a new addition to the family, we'll make sure you've got the most accurate and relevant appliance usage information at your fingertips.
payload.DISAGG101_AIE.ANSWER_3: It sure is! Our disaggregation technology and home assessment survey shows how much you actually use per appliance, not how much a "typical" home should use. You're not a statistic; we won't treat you like one.
payload.DISAGG101_AIE.TEASER_TEXT: Appliance itemization is powered by disaggregation… a process that takes the energy usage data from your meter and uses software algorithms to identify the individual appliances that are actually using the energy.

Itemized costs to operate appliances in your home.

payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.1: What is appliance itemization and how does it work?

Appliance itemization is powered by disaggregation… a process that takes the energy usage data from your meter and uses software algorithms to identify the individual appliances that are actually using the energy.
How can I reduce my cooling usage?

• Set your AC to 24–26°C instead of lower temperatures
  • Use ceiling fans in combination with AC to circulate air
  • Service your AC every 6–12 months to ensure efficiency
  • Invest in inverter-based 5-star ACs or energy-efficient coolers
  • Close curtains/blinds during the day to block heat
  • Turn off ACs and fans when not in use
Does cooling usage depend on where I live?

Yes! Your cooling load is influenced by:

  • Geography: Coastal areas = more humidity → higher AC use.
  • Climate zone: Northern India → seasonal cooling. Southern & Western India → long summers.
  • Home design: Top-floor apartments and poorly ventilated homes retain more heat.
  • Home survey answers: If you selected multiple ACs or cooling appliances in your Home Profile, the system tailors estimates accordingly.
How is cooling usage detected in my home?
Each cooling appliance has a unique energy signature. Our system uses disaggregation technology to recognize when and how long devices like ACs or coolers are running, based on your smart meter data.
How can I see my cooling usage?

Navigate to your portal:

Energy Analytics → Energy Details → Appliance → Year → Click on drop down (All Appliances) → Select (Cooling).

You’ll see trends, comparison with previous periods, and appliance-level breakdown if disaggregation is enabled for your account.
Why does refrigeration matter?

Understand how your fridge or freezer impacts your electricity bill – and how to save.

Why does refrigeration matter?

Refrigerators and freezers run 24/7, all year round, making them one of the most energy-consuming appliances in Indian homes, especially in hot and humid regions like Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, and Mumbai.

If your fridge is over 8 years old, or not energy-efficient, it could be using up to 2× more electricity than a modern one.
What does a 3, 4, or 5-Star BEE rating mean?
India uses BEE Star Ratings (Bureau of Energy Efficiency) to help consumers identify energy-efficient appliances. The more stars, the more energy (and money) you save.

High-rated models typically include:

  • Better insulation to maintain cool temperatures
  • Inverter compressors for energy-efficient, variable-speed operation
  • Smart cooling algorithms for stable temperature control and fewer energy spikes
Why my refrigerator consumption may be high?

Refrigerator consumption may be high due to several reasons. If you are using an older model, especially one without a BEE 4 or 5-star rating, it likely consumes significantly more electricity than newer energy-efficient models. Frequent door openings, overloading, or placing hot food directly inside can also make the compressor work harder, increasing energy usage. Additionally, poor ventilation behind the fridge, worn-out door seals, or high ambient temperatures - common in many parts of India - can force the refrigerator to run more often to maintain cooling. In some cases, if you have a double-door or side-by-side model, or use multiple refrigerators, the combined energy draw can be substantial. You can check your refrigerator’s estimated consumption in the Appliance View section of your portal to monitor trends over time.
How is refrigerator usage calculated in the portal?

Our system uses appliance disaggregation technology to detect usage patterns of refrigerators. It looks at:

  • Constant low-level draw (typical of fridges)
  • Compressor cycling behavior
  • Patterns in your home’s daily base load
What types of water heating appliances are commonly used in households?

Your household may use a variety of water heating appliances depending on location, budget, and family size:

  • Storage Electric Geysers – Most commonly used in urban homes; store 10–25 liters of hot water.
  • Instant Electric Geysers – Heat water on demand; ideal for small families or kitchens.
  • Gas Water Heaters (LPG/PNG) – Often used where electricity is expensive or unreliable.
  • Immersion Rods – Inexpensive and still common in low-income households or rented flats.
  • Solar Water Heaters – Popular in independent houses and societies with rooftop access, especially in sunny regions.
Why is my water heating usage high?

High water heating usage can occur due to:

  • Longer daily showers or multiple family members using hot water
  • Leaving the geyser on continuously, especially storage geysers
  • High-capacity geysers (15L or more) used frequently
  • Old or inefficient models without temperature control
  • Colder climate - in northern India, usage peaks from November to February
  • Poor insulation in pipes or storage tanks
You can check your daily and monthly water heating usage in the Usage Breakdown section of the portal.
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.2: How does it work? Magic?

Not really. Each appliance uses electricity in a unique manner - think of it like an appliance fingerprint. We detect and extract these "fingerprints" and convert the data into useful insights and recommendations.
How does the portal detect my water heating usage?

Each water heating appliance has a unique energy consumption pattern, or “fingerprint.” Our system uses disaggregation technology to detect this pattern and estimate how much of your total energy use comes from water heating.
The more accurate your Home Survey inputs (like geyser type, usage habits), the more precise your breakdown will be.
How much energy does a water heater typically use?

• AppliancePower Rating (Watts): Typical Usage/DayMonthly Energy Use(Approx)
  • Storage Geyser (15L): 2000–3000W | 30–60 mins/day | 30–60 units/month
  • Instant Geyser (3L): 3000W | 15–20 mins/day | 15–30 units/month
  • Gas Heater (LPG): ~1200W (equivalent) | 20–30 mins/day | 1–2 LPG cylinders/month
  • Immersion Rod: 1500W | 30 mins/day | 20–40 units/month
  • Solar Water Heater: Negligible (electric backup only)
Does solar water heating work well in India?

Yes. India receives ample sunlight across most regions, making solar water heaters a reliable and eco-friendly option. They are especially popular in:

  • Independent houses in South and West India
  • Apartment buildings with rooftop access
  • Government or institutional buildings

They provide hot water for free during sunny hours. However, most setups include an electric backup for cloudy days.
What is a BEE star rating for water heaters, and why is it important?

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) rates storage electric geysers on a scale of 1 to 5 stars based on energy efficiency.

  • 5-star models use better insulation and heat retention
  • They consume less electricity per liter of hot water
  • Can save ₹500–₹1000/year in energy costs compared to unrated models
Instant geysers and gas heaters are currently not covered under BEE ratings.
Can I track water heating separately in my portal?

Yes. If water heating has been detected, it will appear as a separate category in the Usage Breakdown section of your portal. If not:

  • Check if you’ve updated your Home Survey with geyser type
  • Ensure your geyser is used consistently for detection
  • Reach out to support if detection is missing
My water heating usage seems incorrect. What should I do?

Here are steps you can take:

  1. Check Home Survey – Make sure geyser or water heater type and usage is filled out correctly.
  2. Review Daily Usage Trends – Sudden spikes may be due to continuous operation or incorrect category detection.
  3. Contact Support – If you believe there is an error in your data, our support team can help re-evaluate your usage pattern.
Can water heating be powered by gas instead of electricity?

Yes. Many Indian homes use LPG or PNG-based water heaters, especially in areas with unstable electricity or high tariffs.

  • They heat water faster
  • Typically cheaper per unit of energy than electricity
  • Must be installed with proper ventilation for safety
These are commonly seen in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and southern states.
How are my tips generated?
Tips are recommended by AI algorithm, which looks at your energy use and home details to share ideas that fit your lifestyle and help you save.
Can I personalize or flag recommendations?
You can refresh your recommendations by updating your home profile. Once you make changes, our system automatically adjusts your appliance details and updates your tips.
What does “Why this is recommended” base its insight on?

All the actions we recommend are personalized for you and based on your data. The “Why this is recommended” section explains why the tip was suggested, how it can help you, and how much you could save by following it.
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.3: What if my usage changes?

Don't worry, we've got you covered. The insights we derive from each appliance in your home will change according to your actual usage patterns. So whether you go on vacation, buy a new appliance, or have a new addition to the family, we'll make sure you've got the most accurate and relevant appliance usage information at your fingertips.
How often are tips updated?
Your tips are updated automatically after each billing cycle when your energy usage data is refreshed, or whenever you make changes to your home profile.
How savings potential is calculated?

Each recommendation we provide is based on typical savings potential derived from standard industry data. We then adjust this using your specific appliance costs to estimate your personalized savings potential.
What are Programs & rebates?

Programs are offered by EnergyCo to help customers make their homes more energy efficient and reduce their energy bills over time. The programs shown on your Savings Hub are those you’re eligible for and can benefit from.
What is the Home Profile Survey and why is it needed?
It’s a short questionnaire about your home (type, size, number of occupants, major appliances like AC/geyser/fridge, tariff plan/slabs, EV/solar, typical schedules).

We use it to:

  • calibrate your appliance itemization (who’s using how much and when),
  • tailor tips & savings estimates to your reality,
  • choose the right similar homes for fair comparisons, and
  • apply the correct rates (₹/kWh, slabs, TOU) when showing costs.
Better profile → more accurate insights.
How do I update my home profile?

• From any chart or the Savings Hub, click Personalize your home profile (or Settings → Home Profile).
  • Edit details and Save. Changes update your itemization, insights, and comparisons within a few minutes.
Tip: If something big changes - new AC, switch to TOU plan, added EV/solar - update your profile to keep results accurate.
How long does it take for changes to my Home Profile to reflect in the itemized usage?

When you update your Home Profile, changes may take up to 24 hours to reflect in your appliance itemization and similar homes comparison. This processing time ensures your data is accurately regrouped and personalized based on your updated inputs.
What is a Budget Alert?

A Budget Alert is a notification that helps you stay on track with your electricity spending. It notifies you when your energy usage in the current billing cycle exceeds a certain percentage of your set budget (75% or 100%). This gives you a chance to adjust your usage before your bill gets too high.
How is the Budget Alert triggered?

The alert is automatically sent when your energy usage for the current bill cycle crosses either:

  • 75% of your set budget (early warning), or
  • 100% of your set budget (budget fully used).
These thresholds help you take timely action to avoid unexpected costs.
How do I set or change my budget?

Yes, you can opt out of receiving this email from the Preferences → Alerts page. Simply uncheck the Bill Projection email option and save your preferences.

You can open it directly here: Preferences → Alerts.
How will I be notified?

You’ll receive a Budget Alert via email and/or SMS, depending on your notification preferences. The message will include:

  • Your usage progress
  • Your set budget
  • Tips to help you manage your usage
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.4: Is my usage unique?

It sure is! Our disaggregation technology and home assessment survey shows how much you actually use per appliance, not how much a "typical" home should use. You're not a statistic; we won't treat you like one.
What should I do if I cross my budget?

Crossing your budget means you're using more energy than planned. You can:

  • Check which appliances are contributing the most to your usage (via the Usage Breakdown page)
  • Reduce high-usage activities or appliances
  • Use personalized energy-saving tips
Can I stop receiving Budget Alerts?
Yes. You can opt out of receiving Budget Alerts anytime from the Notifications Settings page. Just uncheck the option for Budget Alerts and save your preferences.
What is the Bill Projection feature?

The Bill Projection feature provides an estimate of what your electricity bill might be at the end of the current billing cycle, based on your usage so far. You can view your projected bill directly on the Home page of your portal, and you will also receive a Bill Projection email midway through your billing cycle.
Both help you stay informed, plan ahead, and manage your energy usage more effectively.
When is the Bill Projection email sent?

This email is automatically triggered midway through your current billing cycle. It gives you:

  • A projected bill amount
  • How this projection compares to your normal bill
  • The number of days remaining in your billing cycle
How is the projected bill calculated?

The projected bill is estimated using:

  • Your current usage so far in this billing cycle
  • Historical usage patterns (with and without seasonal trends)
  • Typical appliance behavior for your household type
The system recalculates these values for each new billing cycle to keep your projection accurate.
Why is the projected bill higher than usual?

Several reasons may cause a higher projection:

  • Higher than normal appliance usage
  • Seasonal changes (e.g. increased AC use in summer)
  • More people or longer hours at home
  • Older or inefficient appliances consuming more energy
Is the projection always accurate?

While projections are based on your real data and historical patterns, they are still estimates. Actual bills may vary due to:

  • Changes in tariff or taxes
  • Appliance usage spikes
  • Meter sync or data transmission delays
For the most accurate info, keep checking the Usage page and make sure your home profile is up to date.
Can I stop receiving the Bill Projection email?
Yes, you can opt out of receiving this email from the Preferences → Alerts page. Simply uncheck the Bill Projection email option and save your preferences.
What is the Monthly Summary email?

The Monthly Summary email provides a snapshot of your energy usage for the most recent billing period. It includes:

  • Your bill summary (total amount and usage trends)
  • Energy usage breakdown by appliance category
  • Personalized insights and savings tips
  • A usage comparison with previous months
How is the energy usage breakdown calculated?

We analyze your electricity consumption using smart disaggregation algorithms to estimate how much energy each appliance category (like cooling, heating, lighting, etc.) used during your billing period. This helps you better understand where your energy is going.
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.5: What are appliance Itemization Categories?

We itemize your usage into 10 major appliance categories. You can track the usage of every single category over the course of the year and see how they change based on season, weather and your behavior. We display categories that consume a large amount of electricity, like Always On (baseload) and Cooling  based on the usage from your meter. We then take this usage to infer and estimate how much your other appliance categories, like laundry, cooking, lighting and entertainment, are consuming. Thus, through a combination of your actual usage and our rule-based model, we can compose a holistic picture of your total energy consumption.
How are personalized tips generated?

The tips you see are automatically selected based on:

  • Your appliance usage patterns
  • Efficiency opportunities unique to your home
  • High-usage categories in the current or previous billing cycle
Each tip is tailored to help you save energy or improve efficiency.
Can I stop receiving the Monthly Summary email?

Yes. You can manage your preferences and unsubscribe from the email by:

  • Clicking the Unsubscribe link at the bottom of the email
  • Visiting the Notifications Settings page on your portal
What is a billing cycle?

A billing cycle is the time period for which your electricity usage is measured and billed by your utility. Most billing cycles are monthly, but the exact start and end dates may vary depending on your utility provider.
Why don’t my billing cycle dates match a calendar month?
Utilities often have staggered billing cycles to manage operations. Your billing cycle may start or end on any day of the month depending on when your meter is read or when the account was set up.
What is a tariff?

A tariff is the pricing plan set by your utility provider that determines how much you pay for electricity. It may include fixed charges, variable rates based on usage, and sometimes time-of-use pricing.
Where can I find my current tariff plan?
Your tariff information is usually available on your utility bill or utility website. It may also be visible in your energy portal options if your utility has shared that data with us.
What’s the difference between fixed and variable charges?

Fixed Charges: A standard fee you pay each month regardless of usage (e.g., service or meter fees)

Variable Charges: Based on how much electricity you use during the billing cycle.

Some plans may also include additional charges like taxes, regulatory fees, or rebates.
What is time-of-use (TOU) pricing?

Time-of-use pricing means electricity rates change depending on the time of day. Power is usually more expensive during peak demand hours (e.g., evenings) and cheaper during off-peak times (e.g., night or early morning).
Why is my bill amount different from the energy usage shown in the portal?

The energy portal shows your usage-based energy charges only. Your final bill from the utility may include additional charges like:

  • Taxes and fees
  • Fixed monthly service charges
  • One-time adjustments or credits
How is my data used?

We use your energy data and Home Profile to:

  • Show your usage and costs by day, month and year
  • Estimate which appliances use the most
  • Give personalized tips and rebates
  • Improve the accuracy of the service in aggregate (no personal identification)

We do not sell your personal data.
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.6: What's contributing to your ‘Always On’ usage?

Some electrical appliances and electronics continue to draw power even when you’re not actively using them. This is called standby or phantom load, and it contributes to your "Always On" energy usage.

Here’s what could be consuming electricity 24/7 in an average household, along with their impact levels:

High impact (Consumes more electricity constantly)

These appliances draw significant power even in standby mode or because they are always plugged in and running:

  • Set-Top Box (with recording)
  • Wi-Fi Routers and Modems
  • Desktops or Gaming PCs
  • Inverter and Battery Systems (especially during idle charging mode)
  • Aquarium Heaters and Filters
  • Smart TVs (with voice assistant enabled)
  • Microwave Ovens (with clock/display always on)

Medium Impact (Moderate standby consumption)

These devices may not consume a lot on their own, but if left on for long durations or used frequently, their impact adds up:

  • Laptop Chargers (when plugged in 24/7)
  • Refrigerators with Digital Displays
  • Air Purifiers
  • Digital Cable Box (without recording)
  • Audio Systems or Home Theatre Units
  • Smart Speakers (Alexa, Google Home, etc.)

Low Impact (Minimal standby power)

These devices draw very little power individually, but having many can increase your Always On load:

  • Mobile Phone Chargers
  • Electric Toothbrushes
  • LED Clock Radios
  • Wi-Fi Repeaters
  • CCTV/DVR Security Systems
  • Power Tool Batteries (left in charger)
  • Mosquito/Insect Repellents (plug-in devices)
Is my energy usage data private?
Yes. Your data is encrypted in transit and at rest. We follow utility-grade security practices and limit access to authorized staff only.
Who has access to my information?

• You (when signed in).
  • Your utility and our authorized service providers who run this portal - only for operating the service, under strict contracts and confidentiality.
No one else, unless you share it.
How often is my data refreshed?

It depends on your meter and billing setup:

  • Smart meters (5-, 15-, or 60-minute intervals): usage data is usually processed overnight and appears the next day (typical delay 24–48 hours). Some utilities push intraday updates, but it is not real-time: 5-minute granularity does not mean live data.
  • Monthly or bi-monthly reads (no interval data): new usage appears after each bill cycle closes.
  • Bills and charges: update when your utility posts the statement.
  • Tips, itemization and comparisons: refresh whenever new data arrives or when you update your Home Profile.

If something looks missing, it usually fills in within a day or two (meter communications, holidays, or outages can cause short delays). You can always try Refresh and check back later.
What is BEE and why should I care?

BEE (Bureau of Energy Efficiency) is a government agency under the Ministry of Power, responsible for promoting energy conservation in India.

To help consumers make smarter energy choices, BEE runs the Star Labeling Program, which rates appliances from 1-star (least efficient) to 5-star (most efficient).

This helps you:

  • Compare models before buying
  • Save money on long-term electricity bills
  • Reduce your carbon footprint
What does a 5-star rating mean?

A 5-star appliance is one of the most energy-efficient models available in its category. These appliances:
  • Use up to 50% less electricity compared to 1-star models
  • Meet or exceed strict energy-saving standards set by BEE
  • May cost more initially but pay back in savings over time

For example:

  • Refrigerator: Upgrading from a 1-star (around 500 units/year) to a 5-star (around 200–250 units/year) can save about ₹1,500–₹2,000 per year.
  • Air Conditioner (1.5T): Moving from 1-star (around 1,500 units/year) to 5-star (around 900 units/year) can save about ₹4,000–₹6,000 per year.
  • Geyser: Switching from 1-star (around 1,200 units/year) to 5-star (around 600 units/year) can save about ₹2,500 or more per year.
Note: Actual savings depend on usage and electricity tariff in your area.
Which appliances are covered under BEE's Star Label program?

As of 2026, BEE star ratings apply to these commonly used appliances:

  • Refrigerators
  • Air conditioners (Split & Window)
  • Washing machines
  • Televisions
  • Water heaters (Geysers)
  • Ceiling fans
  • LED lamps
  • Inverters/UPS systems
  • Electric motors
  • Chillers
  • Microwave ovens (Voluntary)
  • Laptops (Voluntary)

You can check the full list at beeindia.gov.in.
Where can I see the star rating on a product?

Look for the Star Label sticker on the appliance. It includes:
  • Number of stars (1–5)
  • Annual energy consumption (in kWh)
  • BEE logo and certification number
  • Validity date

Check if the star rating is valid: some appliances have expired stickers from previous years. Star ratings get stricter each year – always look for the latest label.
Why are 5-star appliances worth it?

• Lower electricity bills
  • Better performance
  • Environmentally friendly operation
  • Longer appliance life
  • Government-certified savings

Even if the upfront cost is higher, 5-star appliances usually recover their price difference within 1–2 years due to energy savings.
Where can I buy 5-star appliances?
Most major brands in India - LG, Samsung, Voltas, Blue Star, Haier, IFB, Whirlpool, etc. - offer 5-star models.

Buy from:

  • Authorised brand showrooms
  • Large retailers like Reliance Digital, Croma, etc.
  • Online marketplaces like Amazon and Flipkart (look for “5-star BEE rated” in the product specs)

What is Water Heating?

Water heating is a major contributor to energy consumption in Indian households, especially during winter months or in colder regions like North India, or hill states such as Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. This FAQ will help you understand what drives your water heating usage, how it’s measured, and what options are available for reducing your energy bills.

What appliances are included in the "Other Appliances" category?
These are appliances that are too small or infrequently used to be categorized separately. This includes mobile phones, vacuum cleaners, hair dryers, and curling irons.
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.8: What appliances are included in the "Cooling" category?

The “Cooling” category includes all appliances used to reduce indoor temperatures. In India, the most common ones are:

  • High - Split AC (inverter or non-inverter), Window AC, Heat Pumps (cooling mode), VRF/VRV systems.
  • Medium - Air coolers (desert/personal), Tower/portable AC.
  • Low - Ceiling fans, Table/Wall/Pedestal fans.
  • Minimal - Exhaust fans (bathroom/kitchen).
payload.com.bidgely.cloud.faq.GLOBAL.questions.9: Why my cooling consumption is high?

Your cooling usage may spike due to:

  • Extended usage hours during summer or heatwaves
  • Low efficiency appliances (e.g. non-inverter ACs)
  • Improper room insulation (hot air leaks in, cool air escapes)
  • Frequent switching on/off instead of maintaining temp
  • AC temperature set too low (e.g., 18°C instead of 24°C)
  • Multiple fans and coolers running together
  • Old or unmaintained appliances (dirty filters or gas leaks)
